item.title: Incarico post-doc: Chemical Characterization and Biological Activity of Bioactive Compounds from Zygophyllum oxianum (Univ. TUSCIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 23:59
Institution: Univ. TUSCIA, Viterbo
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-01 Botanica

The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to the characterization of bioactive metabolites from *Zygophyllum oxianum*, with particular focus on triterpene glycosides and flavonoids, and to the analysis and profiling of these compounds using chromatographic and spectrometric techniques. They will assess the biological activity of selected extracts, fractions and compounds in human cell models by measuring cell viability and EC₅₀ values, investigating effects on the cell cycle, cell death and oxidative stress, and contributing to imaging studies and validation of the results in three-dimensional cell models.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: The reduction of NMDA receptor Ca2+ permeability as a strategyto lower neuronal vulnerability to excitotoxicity (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-05 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The scientific activities within the scope of this project will involve designing and implementing experiments to measure the Ca²⁺ permeability of human NMDA-type glutamate receptors expressed in heterologous systems under different conditions and in the presence of various pharmacological modulators. The methods employed will include patch-clamp electrophysiological recording techniques combined with time-resolved digital fluorescence microscopy, allowing simultaneous monitoring of Ca²⁺ inward currents and changes in intracellular free Ca²⁺ concentration.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-02 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Rome
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-12 Anatomia umana

Study of the contribution of peripheral nerves to processes of neovascularisation associated with tumour growth, through structural, ultrastructural and immunohistochemical analyses in experimental models and in humans. The role of Schwann cells within the tumour microenvironment in liver cancer and melanoma will be analysed. The project will focus on the capacity of Schwann cells in modulating tumour angiogenesis and vascular mimicry which are essential steps in governing tumour growth, survival and invasion.

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Study of the role of membrane potential in the regulation of cell fate and function, using integrated optogenetic and electrophysiological methodologies. (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-18 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Roma
Field: Biology / 05/BIOS-06 Fisiologia

The researcher will investigate membrane potential as an instructive signal in the regulation of cell fate and function, employing integrated optogenetic and electrophysiological methodologies. The work will involve developing and applying protocols to modulate membrane potential through acute and chronic optogenetic stimulation, combined with intracellular (patch-clamp) and extracellular (multi-electrode array, MEA) electrophysiological recordings. Using neuronal and cardiac models, the project aims to assess how the modulation of membrane potential contributes to processes such as differentiation, functional maturation, and integration into pre-existing cellular networks.
